item.title: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78755-8

Skin-attached devices can easily inflame or collapse. Here, the authors show a multi-lobed microneedle device that holds micron-scale conduits open for seven days, allowing repeated protein sampling from interstitial fluid

item.title: Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79329-4

Rafeh et al. use frequency-tagged fMRI to demonstrate that selective attention relies on dual, independent neural mechanisms for target enhancement and surround suppression, elaborating on traditional unitary models of human visual attention.
item.dc:title: Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression

item.title: Functionally divergent RHOA mutations drive peripheral T cell lymphoma development by engaging a common neomorphic pathway
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79260-8

RHOA mutation variants, exerting opposite effects on canonical RHOA signaling, are associated with peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCL). Here, the authors show that different RHOA mutants share a neomorphic activity that activates the transcription factor NFAT to drive PTCL.
item.dc:title: Functionally divergent RHOA mutations drive peripheral T cell lymphoma development by engaging a common neomorphic pathway

item.title: UMIche: a UMI-centric analysis platform for enhancing molecular quantification accuracy in bulk and single-cell sequencing
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79336-5

Errors in unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) can distort molecule counts. Here, the authors present UMIche, a platform for benchmarking deduplication methods, and show that set cover and majority voting are more robust as barcode errors increase.
item.dc:title: UMIche: a UMI-centric analysis platform for enhancing molecular quantification accuracy in bulk and single-cell sequencing

item.title: Toward triggered generation of indistinguishable single photons from MoTe<sub>2</sub> quantum emitters
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78808-y

Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides are promising single-photon platforms but achieving photon indistinguishability remains challenging. Here, the authors realize reproducible near-infrared quantum emitters in bilayer MoTe2 with high purity, electrical tunability, and record indistinguishability.
item.dc:title: Toward triggered generation of indistinguishable single photons from MoTe<sub>2</sub> quantum emitters

item.title: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79063-x

OsPUB2 degrades OsPUB12 to promote rice immunity. Phosphorylation of OsPUB12 by OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 at two sites fine-tunes its stability and the plant’s defense response.
item.dc:title: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity

item.title: Low-thermal-budget solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric for low-voltage 2D electronics
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79139-8

The low temperature synthesis of high-quality dielectrics is desired for the development of 2D electronics. Here, the authors report an environmentally friendly synthesis method of solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric layers and their application for low-voltage 2D transistors and logic circuits.
item.dc:title: Low-thermal-budget solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric for low-voltage 2D electronics

item.title: Ferrocene heteroconjugation enables charge transport in DNA monolayers
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79212-2

DNA is a promising self-assembling material for molecular electronics, but efficient charge injection remains challenging because of its deep HOMO energy level. Here, the authors develop a chemically defined DNA–ferrocene conjugate through covalent modification of a DNA duplex and demonstrate an enhanced electrical response. The resulting metal–DNA molecular junctions show how electronic functionality can be programmed by molecular design, providing a platform for quantitative comparison with theoretical models.
item.dc:title: Ferrocene heteroconjugation enables charge transport in DNA monolayers
